title: The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
paragraphs: Douglas Adams's BBC science-fiction comedy follows the bewildered Arthur Dent after Earth is destroyed, sending him across the galaxy with Ford Prefect and an increasingly improbable group of companions.

The first 12 Fits originate as radio drama; later phases adapt later novels. Frozen titles are book/part labels and are retained while canonical Fit aliases and original BBC dates are added as research evidence.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Primary Phase (March 8, 1978 to April 12, 1978) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]], Secondary Phase (December 24, 1978 to January 25, 1980) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]], Tertiary Phase (September 21, 2004 to October 26, 2004) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]], and Quandary Phase (May 3, 2005 to May 24, 2005) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Douglas Adams (source author, writer, and additional material), Dirk Maggs (radio adaptor and director), Geoffrey McGivern (performer), Paddy Kingsland (music), Peter Jones (performer), Simon Jones (performer), and Geoffrey Perkins (producer).
The stories often return to interstellar travel and cosmic scale, The Hitchhiker's Guide and information systems, absurdist science-fiction comedy, and Earth, destruction and reconstruction.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes 1978 BBC Radio 4 science-fiction comedy launch, Secondary Phase completion, 2004-2005 radio revival and novel adaptations, and 2018 fortieth-anniversary Hexagonal Phase.
